overview:
Massachusetts' ninth district leans Democratic, and incumbent Bill Keating enters the general election with the advantages that usually decide races like this. He has roughly half a million dollars on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has about thirty-five thousand, limiting the challenger's ability to introduce himself to voters. No public polls of the race are available, and no professional race raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets put Keating's chances around 95%, and the district's fundamentals point the same way: a Democratic-leaning electorate plus a standard incumbency edge. The expectation is a comfortable double-digit win for Keating, with the main source of uncertainty the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability. A late surge in challenger spending or attention would be the most plausible way the race tightens.
